Acclaimed author Jan Notzon will join Texas A&M International University students for a moderated conversation about his background, writing process and the inspiration behind his work, according to TAMIU.

The event is open to the TAMIU community and is scheduled for Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, at 3:20 p.m. in the Academic Innovation Center, room 125. The conversation was made possible through the generosity of Sonia and Memo Benavides, longtime TAMIU partners and Laredo philanthropists, according to the university.

Notzon is a Laredo native, novelist, playwright, actor and founder of the Laredo Little Theatre. His work explores themes of family, faith, identity and the Texas-Mexico border, TAMIU said. That includes “Only the Dead (Know the End of War),” which follows two Mexican families and one Anglo family amid the formation of the Mexican and Texas republics, and “The Dogs...Barking,” a coming-of-age story set in a 1950s Texas border town.

He has written seven full-length plays and a one-act play produced in New York City, according to TAMIU. His play “When Good Men Do Nothing” was a finalist in San Francisco’s Dramarama Competition, and his other works include the children’s story “The Gift of Arbol Ceiba.” As an actor, Notzon has appeared in television productions including “Matlock,” “The Young Indiana Jones Chronicles” and Hallmark Channel’s “The Confession.”

For more information, TAMIU lists the College of Arts and Sciences at 956.326.2462 or coas@tamiu.edu.

Sources:

  • Texas A&M International University, “TAMIU Invites Author Jan Notzon to Campus for Curated Conversation on Writing Process,” Oct. 29, 2026
